name: map_prime_of_equiv
script:
intro h
have h₁ : ∃ (T : Type u_4) [inst : CommRing T] [IsDedekindDomain T], True := by
  refine' ⟨ℤ, inferInstance, inferInstance, _⟩
  trivial
obtain ⟨T, inst, IsDedekindDomain.T, h₂⟩ := h₁
have h₃ := h (T := T) (inst := inst) (IsDedekindDomain.T := IsDedekindDomain.T) (R := T) (inst_2 := inst) (IsDedekindDomain.R := IsDedekindDomain.T)
  (f := 1 : T ≃+* T) (I := ⊤ : Ideal T)
have h₄ : Prime (⊤ : Ideal T) → (⊤ : Ideal T) ≠ ⊥ → Prime (Ideal.map (1 : T ≃+* T) ⊤) := by
  intro h₅ h₆
  simpa [h₆] using h₃ h₅ h₆
have h₅ : ¬Prime (⊤ : Ideal T) := by
  have h₅₁ : ¬Prime (⊤ : Ideal T) := by
    intro h₅₂
    -- Prove that the ideal ⊤ is not prime in a Dedekind domain
    have h₅₃ := IsDedekindDomain.T.ne_zero_iff.mpr (by infer_instance)
    have h₅₄ : Prime (⊤ : Ideal T) → False := by
      intro h₅₅
      -- Use the fact that ⊤ is not a prime ideal in a Dedekind domain
      have h₅₆ := IsDedekindDomain.T.exists_prime_iff.mpr ⟨⟨1, 0⟩, by simp [h₅₁]⟩
      obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := h₅₆
      have h₅₇ : p ⊆ ⊤ := by simp [Ideal.subset_top]
      have h₅₈ : p = ⊤ := by
        apply le_antisymm
        · -- Prove that p ≤ ⊤
          exact h₅₇
        · -- Prove that ⊤ ≤ p
          have h₅₉ := hp.2
          simp_all [Ideal.le_top_iff]
          <;> aesop
      rw [h₅₈] at h₅₅
      simp_all [Prime.ne_bot, Ideal.ne_bot]
    exact h₅₄ h₅₂
  exact h₅₁
have h₆ : (⊤ : Ideal T) ≠ ⊥ := by
  intro h₆₁
  have h₆₂ := IsDedekindDomain.T.ne_zero_iff.mpr (by infer_instance)
  simp_all [Ideal.ext_iff]
  <;> aesop
have h₇ := h₄
simp_all [h₅, h₆]
<;> aesop

name: ZFSet.isOrdinal_toZFSet
script:
have h_main : ∃ (o : Ordinal.{u_1}), ¬ (o.toZFSet.IsOrdinal) := by
  use ⟨0, by trivial⟩
  -- We choose `o = 0` as our counterexample.
  -- The set of elements in `o` is empty, so it cannot be an ordinal.
  have h₁ : ((⟨0, by trivial⟩ : Ordinal.{u_1}).toZFSet : Set ℕ) = ∅ := by
    simp [Ordinal.toZFSet]
    <;> aesop
  -- We need to show that the set of elements in `o` is not an ordinal.
  have h₂ : ¬ ((⟨0, by trivial⟩ : Ordinal.{u_1}).toZFSet).IsOrdinal := by
    rw [h₁]
    intro h
    -- If it were an ordinal, there would be some element in the empty set, which is a contradiction.
    exact Set.not_nonempty_empty (by simpa using h.1)
  exact h₂

-- Using the main statement, we can now prove the theorem.
intro h
obtain ⟨o, ho⟩ := h_main
have h₁ : o.toZFSet.IsOrdinal := h o
contradiction

  intro h₃
  have h₄ : (0 : ℝ) < 1 := by norm_num

  intro h₄

    exact h₂ h₄
  | inr h₄ =>
    have h₅ : (1 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) := by
      rw [h₄]
      norm_num
    norm_num at h₅

  intro h₆
  have h₇ : (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = ∅ ∨ (Set.Iio (0 : ℝ) : Set ℝ) = Set.univ := by
    exact h₄.mp h₆
